t:
Title 10, United States Code, is amended as follows:
    (1)
        (A) Section 232 is repealed. 
        (B) The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 9 is amended by striking the item relating to section 232.  
    (2) Section 2859(d) is amended—
        (A) by striking paragraph (2); and 
        (B) by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (2).  
    (3) Section 10503(13)(B) is amended—
        (A) by striking clause (iii); and 
        (B) redesignating clause (iv) as clause (iii).

fable.w: This section only makes technical and conforming amendments to Title 10: it repeals one section, strikes paragraphs and clauses, and redesignates others. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. There is no tempting participation reading, since the text names no actors or decision process at all.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the United States Code, specifically repealing sections and redesignating paragraphs and clauses. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, comment periods, or rights to sue mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Title 10, United States Code, is amended as follows: (1) (A) Section 232 is repealed. (B) The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 9 is amended by striking the item relating to section 232. (2) Section 2859(d) is amended— (A) by striking paragraph (2); and (B) by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (2). (3) Section 10503(13)(B) is amended— (A) by striking clause (iii); and (B) redesignating clause (iv) as clause (iii).

opus.w: The section only makes technical changes: it repeals section 232, strikes a paragraph and a clause, and renumbers what follows. Nothing in the text creates any process involving states, tribes, the public, experts or other outside parties in a federal decision. Guessing at what the repealed provisions said is not a basis for finding participation in this text.
opus.b: This section only repeals or strikes provisions of Title 10 and renumbers what remains. The text never says what the repealed provisions contained. One could guess that a repealed section or struck paragraph involved consultation or hearings. But nothing in the text itself mentions anyone outside the federal government taking part in a federal decision. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the United States Code, such as repealing sections, striking paragraphs, and redesignating clauses. It does not create any advisory committees, require public comment, mandate consultation with non-federal entities, or grant rights to sue. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Title 10, United States Code, is amended as follows: (1) (A) Section 232 is repealed. (B) The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 9 is amended by striking the item relating to section 232. (2) Section 2859(d) is amended— (A) by striking paragraph (2); and (B) by redesignating paragraph (3) as paragraph (2). (3) Section 10503(13)(B) is amended— (A) by striking clause (iii); and (B) redesignating clause (iv) as clause (iii).
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that repealing or amending sections could implicitly remove or add participation requirements, but the text itself does not describe any participatory process. It is purely a technical amendment to the code structure.
Resolution: The section only lists technical amendments (repeals, redesignations, striking clauses) to Title 10 of the U.S. Code. It does not establish any new advisory bodies, comment periods, consultations with outside parties, or rights to sue. It is purely structural.
